Sample.evidence_source: Two studies (Ns = 238, 288) indicated that it contained two factors (restrictive/critical messages and pressure to eat messages) and yielded internally consistent, stable, and valid scores.

Number of studies.evidence_source: Two studies (Ns = 238, 288) indicated that it contained two factors (restrictive/critical messages and pressure to eat messages) and yielded internally consistent, stable, and valid scores.

section_summary.extract_value: This abstract reports the development of the Caregiver Eating Messages Scale and presents results from two studies (Ns = 238, 288) indicating two factors (restrictive/critical messages and pressure to eat). Findings indicate both factors were positively related to women's BMI and restrictive/critical messages were positively related to men's BMI; restrictive/critical messages predicted lower perceived familial body acceptance, lower intuitive eating, higher perceived familial pressure to be lean, and higher disordered eating, and uniquely predicted men's body appreciation. The abstract explicitly states there were two studies but provides no sample demographics, survey method, exact BMI means, or correlation coefficients.
section_summary.evidence_source: Abstract sentences: 'The Caregiver Eating Messages Scale was developed to measure this construct. Two studies (Ns = 238, 288) indicated that it contained two factors (restrictive/critical messages and pressure to eat messages) and yielded internally consistent, stable, and valid scores.' and 'Both factors were positively related to women's BMI, and restrictive/critical messages were positively related to men's BMI.'
